notes.title: The Button Effect - Game Announcement
notes.content:
Hi there!

Today's a big day for me. I've just announced the trailer and title for my new game: The Button Effect

After over a year of secretly, quietly working on this new project in Unreal Engine 5, the Steam store-page is now live for wishlisting. If you've enjoyed my previous project, Imagine Lifetimes, this one is something completely different. I've wanted to use my background in Architectural Engineering within my games for a long time now, so I've finally made the switch to 3D by picking up UE5 in the past years.

What makes this project so different?

 Genre: It's a first-person puzzler (The Witness, The Talos Principle, but on smaller scale).
 Engine: It's a 3D project made in Unreal Engine 5.
 Tone: It's based on a calmer, more gentle and optimistic perspective on life.

That doesn't mean there aren't any similarities to be found though! I'm working with voice-actors again, the musician that created the Imagine Lifetimes soundtrack is doing the music, it's going to be a shorter bite-sized experience and there's lots of hidden metaphors throughout this new game.

I know Imagine Lifetimes wasn't perfect or what some players expected from it. I like to think I've learned a lot from all of your feedback to improve my overall game design. It's been a while since you've heard from me here, but I'm hoping you'll be curious to check out my new project?

You can follow my Steam developer profile to keep an eye on everything I do in the future.

If minimalist first-person puzzlers happen to be your thing, wishlist The Button Effect on Steam.

Thanks for all of your support,
- Tim (Frycandle)

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Language Update 2.0.3
notes.content:
Hey Steam!

It's been quite some time since the last update, but we've added 3 new languages to the game!

In-game translation options are now available for:
- English
- Dutch
- Spanish (NEW)
- Brazilian Portuguese (NEW)
- Greek  (NEW)

Community translators have been working tirelessly in the background to provide full in-game translations of all subtitles and texts in Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese and Greek!

This was my first release, so I naturally underestimated the sheer volume of work required to add new languages to the game. Huge shout-out to the community translators involved! The amount of dedication and effort it took to translate every single line of text in the game to another language is just incredible.

CREDITS:

TheFastSpace - Spanish translations
Kauã Francisco Moreira - Brazilian Portuguese translations
Bamb8s - Greek translations

In addition, I'd like to thank you all once again for playing the game. It means a lot to me that you were there to support something I've created. (if you are able to leave a review, that'd be tremendously helpful) I'm in the middle of learning how to create 3D games, which is something I'd love to pursue in the future.

Cheers,
- Tim (Frycandle)

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Patch 2.0.2
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/6f4ba5fb013d6b556a4bcf167d6dac5024abdc77.png

Hey Steam!

This tiny patch is geared towards improving replay-ability for you, allowing you to skip (optional) through the opening credits. These are simple additions, but hopefully they will make your life a bit easier! :)

Most of these hints / skips will only become visible after having at least one ending completed. It made sense to apply this requirement because some things are best not skipped on your very first play. 


 You can now press ENTER during the opening credits to skip ahead
(you will see a hint for this during the opening credits after having at least 1 ending completed)

 You can now press ENTER during any of the egg-cell fertilization sequences to skip ahead
(you can also click on the fast-forward button during any of the egg-cell fertilization sequences)

 You are no longer required to read the content warning after having at least 1 ending completed


Last but not least, you'll notice a teeny tiny visual change inside the light-bulb. Clicking the light-bulb inside the imagination menu (brain) will take you to the hidden backstory. This feature wasn't obvious enough so from now it includes a small arrow animation pointing upwards... *hint-hint!*

Go check it out, only 1% of all total players has uncovered the true ending and finale credits so far! :)

Cheers,
-Tim (Frycandle)

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Patch 2.0.1
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/36680d4081b018810bce72fdae30cda6fb7dec9f.png

Hey Steam!

The first 24 hours of the Imagine Lifetimes release are almost behind us. Thank you all so much for the support so far. The game seems stable and no bugs have been reported so far, that's great news!

Based on a handful of reviews, the average playtime and % unlocked of certain achievements, this patch solves some simple but important design flaws. Data shows that when players reach their first ending they assume they've completed the game and quit early. This is a design flaw, because the game has multiple endings (20) and is meant to be played and explored on loop.

With each new ending unlocked, new paths become available throughout and the content intensifies.

The retirement path and ending seemed to be the main culprit. Here's some small but vital fixes:

 The achievement for this ending unlocked too early prior to dying, this is now fixed
 After completing this ending a text will be displayed (Ending 1/20) indicating your progress
 If you press quit [X] or clear [C] during this ending sequence, you will skip ahead and be reborn
 Once reborn, clicking anything will unlock your imagination, a vital part of the game

From now on, as long as you have at least 1 ending completed, you will definitely be able to find the imagination (brain). This is where all your progress is stored, displaying all your completed endings, secrets and challenges. You'll also be able to uncover the main backstory cut-scenes in this menu.

Hopefully these fixes will improve the experience for you. Thank you for your honest feedback and please do keep sending me your thoughts. Your reviews are extremely valuable for the growth of this game. 

If you've played and experienced a good chunk of the game, please consider leaving your review.

Cheers,
-Tim (Frycandle)

P.S. Special thanks to the ZFAM for waiting on this update! <3

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Achievements Reveal
notes.content:
Hey Steam!

With the game's launch window now set for Autumn 2020, I wanted to give you a little sneak peek at some of the new stuff I've been adding to the game. This week's reveal is about... achievements! :)

Imagine Lifetimes is a satirical life-simulator in which you make choices and take various paths to find answers. More specifically, you'll find answers to existential questions like 'What is your purpose?'. As you explore and experiment with each lifetime, you will come across one of the (20) multiple endings.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/82bb4aed275192d3fefa4d45f72b0b954305863d.png

After completing your very first ending, you will be able to unlock your 'Imagination' by clicking on the pacifier in the 'Choose your first words.' screen at the start of the game. This will then expose your brain, clicking it will take you deep into the darkest corners of your mind. It is the place where all your progress is stored: every ending, secret and challenge completed. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/4bd9828516c10403cbab0b00bfe680992c901fd5.png

With 20 unique endings, and 19 additional secrets and challenges, you'll be able to explore and unlock a total of 39 achievements! Each completed ending will be a new piece of the puzzle, unlocking a series of cut-scenes slowly revealing the game's true meaning and backstory.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/5e1de799ce874070b23d3adc18551c1e78187a48.png

If you manage to find at least 17 endings, you'll be able to enter the game's twentieth ending and finale... 

That story finale is my best kept secret, a twist, inspired by deeply personal experiences. I'm convinced it will completely shake your perspectives on what 'Imagine Lifetimes' is all about. I can't wait to show you!

Thank you for being here, you can Wishlist the game on Steam to stay tuned!
- Tim (Frycandle)

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Launch Delay
notes.content:
Hey Steam, after close consideration I have (unfortunately) decided to postpone the Imagine Lifetimes release date to 'Autumn 2020'. My apologies, I've taken the time to explain in more detail below. <3

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/ec0254a63def7e5b4493859c254e541ae998e3d3.png

First of all, I'm sorry for the hype these past few weeks. Please know that it was well meant. It just goes to show how much I believed I had this, I really thought I did. I know some of you have been waiting for months or even years to play the full version of the game. I want to thank you for sticking with me all this time, and I hope that you’ll be here for the last stretch of my journey as well.

Over the years of being a solo game developer one tip I’ve read a thousand times over is this: “Do not underestimate the last 10% of development.” Despite having read it over and over, I still failed to grasp its importance...

I get it now, but it seems I had to learn this one the hard way. I underestimated the final stretch, but also the time it takes to single-handedly release a game. I set the September release date at the start of this year as a goal, to motivate and force myself to work towards a launch day. This has been extremely good for me, as I’ve never been more focused on getting things done as much as I have this year. Unfortunately, as the actual date crept closer, I did not want to admit that it was going to be too tight of a squeeze.

I wish I had the knowledge and experience to make this call sooner. Believe me, this whole thing has been one big learning experience for me. It’s my first release, and without a doubt one of the hardest things I’ll ever do. This week has been the tipping point for me though.

Here’s the thing, I work 32 hours a week as a building engineer. This work takes place at my computer at home, due to COVID, at the same desk I do my game-development work. When I finish work on evenings or in the weekends, I never truly ‘leave’ this desk. Instead I spend more of my time sitting on that same chair, working on what I am passionate about. I have recently taken 5 weeks of holiday leave, not to rest, but to work on my game.

Do not get me wrong, I love it. I work hard because I believe in my project, it is the best thing that ever happened to me, creatively speaking. Unfortunately, no matter how passionate I am, there will always be boundaries to how much I can get done within a certain amount of time. Whether it’s for work or my personal stuff, whenever I’m trying to wrap my head around an impossible deadline, it tends to triggers my migraines.

I had a migraine this week, which is the equivalent of my body saying: NOPE.

Imagine Lifetimes development is about 97.5% there. I’m currently working on adding things like the main menu, achievements and the unlockable main story-line cutscenes. I need to add audio to a couple of endings, tie it all together, and the game is ‘done’. It does not sound like a lot, but it adds up. I was trying to squeeze all that into the next two weeks, I shouldn’t.

Not only would I not be able to give it the finishing touch it deserves, I would have jeopardized the quality of my big finale. Everything I’ve worked for these past four years leads up to this moment, it would be such a shame to rush all that just to make it to my self-imposed deadline. I want to keep the quality consistent, I want things to be stable, and most importantly I want to be alive when I finally release my game.

I hope you all agree. <3

In addition to the actual ‘game development’, know that I’ve got plenty of other tasks I do not want to rush or skip out on. This includes everything marketing related, from updating my press-kit, website and game-page to preparing promotional content for social media. There's a lot of 'hidden' work left to do!

The new date is not set in stone to avoid future disappointment, I do not want to make the same mistake twice. I have called it ‘Autumn 2020’, which I consider to be either October or November at the latest. Here's what I'll do:

- I’m going to finish the game.
- I’m going to polish it.
- I’m going to do proper testing to make for a smooth and stable release.
- I’m going to do all of the above in a healthy way.

Once I am 99.9% confident that I am ready for launch, I will announce the date.

Thank you all for being here, I hope you'll understand and please do stay tuned!
- Tim / Frycandle

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Interactive Devlog
notes.content:
Hey Steam,

My name is Tim, and I'm the solo game developer responsible for the existential rollercoaster known as  'Imagine Lifetimes'. (COMING SOON) As I am currently 100% focusing on finalizing the game's build for it's full release on September 25th, I have to confess I struggle to find time for community interaction.

So, in an attempt to catch up, let's interact!

- How do you like your life-simulators?
- What are your impressions of the game so far? 
- Is there anything I can improve on in terms of store-page presentation?

That's a couple of potential questions to get you warmed up, but please know that games are made by real human beings. These human beings, despite being extremely busy, would love to connect with you!

Here's a link to the Imagine Lifetimes Discord, feel free to shoot me a message at any given time.

In other news: we are now approximately 1 MONTH away from launch day! (HYPE)

Cheers,
- Tim (Frycandle)
